This week on All Songs Considered , NPR Music’s Ann Powers and Isabella Gomez Sarmiento join host Robin Hilton to break down how we’ve reached this point, what it means, and where we go from here. items.desc: The title track ‘Run For Cover’ taps into the wide-eyed escapism of the mid-’90s without slipping into nostalgia. Psychedelic details flicker across the drums like LED trails in a dark room, while a restless walking bassline gives the whole thing a wonderfully physical pull. Elements drift in and out of focus, resisting an obvious genre tag while maintaining an easy, heads-down momentum. It’s progressive music in the literal sense: constantly moving, never particularly interested in announcing where it’s going next.
items.title: [PREVIEW] Nick Warren - Run For Cover

items.desc: On “Stupa”, the mood opens outward. There’s an unmistakable Balearic quality to its sun-warmed percussion and serrated bassline,a groove that immediately suggests open-air dancefloors and late-afternoon light. A woozy synth gradually sends proceedings into more narcotic territory, while soft vocal fragments, keyboard flourishes and flashes of guitar keep one foot planted somewhere recognisably human. Nothing is hurried or overplayed. Instead, Warren lets each element breathe, resulting in the kind of patient, transportive dance music that comes from knowing exactly how little you need to do.
items.title: [PREVIEW] Nick Warren - Stupa

bbc-6-musics-rave-forever.about: A wall-to-wall celebration of dance music from across the decades.

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 12 Jan. Cruise through the history of GTA's iconic gaming soundtrack, from past to present. Across three decades, GTA Radio's iconic stations have become a definitive time capsule of club culture, curated by some global heavyweights like The Blessed Madonna, Soulwax, Solomun, and Gilles Peterson. Dial into the sounds of Jaydee, Ron Trent, PinkPantheress, Major Lazer, Jayda G, and Todd Terje on a journey spanning Acid House, Techno, Nu-Disco, Hardcore, Trance, Latin Electronic and beyond. A We Are Grape production for BBC 6 Music.
items.title: Ravin' To GTA Radio

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 5 Jan. Journey through house and techno as the queen of the dance floor, Honey Dijon, puts her unmistakable stamp on some golden tracks. A Chicago-born, Grammy-winning DJ, producer, activist, and fashion icon, Dijon embodies the pure, unadulterated spirit of house music. You can expect to hear glittering reworks of tracks from Neneh Cherry, 702, Dua Lipa, Madonna, DJ Minx and lots more. A We Are Grape production for BBC 6 Music.
items.title: The Art Of Remixing: Honey Dijon

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 29 Dec. As 6 Music Goes Dark we celebrate two decades of Skream’s seminal debut album with a deep dive into the darkest, moodiest dubstep 2006 had to offer. Expect cuts from the album alongside classic tracks from the likes of Mala, Kode9, Digital Mystikz, Coki and lots more A We Are Grape production for BBC 6 Music.
items.title: 20 Years Of Skream!

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 22 Dec. Cruise through a selection of classic US house anthems. Essential house tracks from the likes of Marshall Jefferson, Aly-Us, Sandy Rivera and Barbara Tucker. A We Are Grape production for BBC 6 Music.

She's also got music from Philip George as her Future Dance Track ID, and new releases from ROKAR, Mad.Again, Sam Girling, ATRIP, Saint Ludo and Burnski. Produced by We Are Grape for BBC Radio 1.
items.title: Papa Nugs in the mix!

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 30 Nov. All the hottest new and emerging dance sounds with Dutch DJ Julian Fijma in the mix! Plus Sarah has new music from O'Flynn as her Future Dance Track ID! Produced by We Are Grape for BBC Radio 1.

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 23 Nov. Sarah has new music from Joshua James as the Future Dance Track ID, and Berlin's Khadija is in the studio for Peak Time Mix! Produced by We Are Grape for BBC Radio 1.

bbc-sherelle.about: Showcasing the best blend of jungle, footwork, breakbeat and a few classics thrown in.

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 15 Dec. Pioneering British techno musician Dave Angel brings a deep techno energy to the Sweatbox. Produced by We Are Grape for BBC Radio 6 Music.
items.title: The Sweatbox - with Dave Angel

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 15 Dec. Sounds combining jazz, house and techno dominate this show as SHERELLE soundtracks Saturday night. Featuring music from Jeff Mills, Juan Atkins, DJ Deeon, Skee Mask and more. SHERELLE also dives into music from this week’s Sweatbox guest, Dave Angel, selecting tracks from his new album A Time and Place. Produced by We Are Grape for BBC Radio 6 Music.
items.title: Down deep

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 8 Dec. London-via-Los Angeles DJ and producer Carré brings her bass-heavy sounds to the Sweatbox. Celebrating a recent EP release on British dubstep label Tempa, Carré weaves between leftfield techno, bass and more in this atmospheric mix. Produced by We Are Grape for BBC Radio 6 Music.
items.title: The Sweatbox - with Carré

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 8 Dec. SHERELLE invites rising Swedish singer, songwriter and producer DJ Suzy into the Cab. DJ Suzy’s music sits between alternative R&B, dream-pop and electronic influences, and SHERELLE sets the scene accordingly with music from Tirzah and Jadu Heart. Later in the show, the music ramps up as the Sweatbox draws closer. Produced by We Are Grape for BBC Radio 6 Music.
items.title: DJ Suzy in the Cab to the Club

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 1 Dec. One for your bass bins: dubstep legend Coki enters the Sweatbox for Halloween, providing 30 minutes of head-rattling bass music. Produced by We Are Grape for BBC Radio 6 Music.
items.title: The Sweatbox - with Coki

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 1 Dec. SHERELLE gets spooky for Halloween, playing the deepest, darkest dubstep in her arsenal! Expect tunes from Mala, multiple appearances from Kahn and Joker, with some haunting sounds along the way... Produced by We Are Grape for BBC Radio 6 Music.
items.title: It's Halloween! Let's Listen To Dubstep!

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 24 Nov. BRIT and MOBO-nominated artist Eliza Rose closes out the Black History Month series in the Sweatbox, with 30 minutes of her favourite UK garage bangers. Produced by We Are Grape for BBC Radio 6 Music.
items.title: The Sweatbox - with Eliza Rose

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 24 Nov. In this all-out celebration of the women of UK garage, Kele Le Roc gets in the Cab to the Club, selecting three tracks she wants to hear en-route to the rave. Elsewhere in the show, SHERELLE's celebrating the often unsung female vocalists, producers and DJs within the genre, with a contributing voice note from Eliza Rose and more. Produced by We Are Grape for BBC Radio 6 Music.
items.title: Celebrating the women of UK garage

bbc-stuart-maconies-freak-zone.about: Adventures in underground and experimental music. A partner to the Freak Zone Playlist.

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 16 Dec. Welcome to the Freak Zone, your bespoke guide to the world of weird and wonderful music. Come for Anna Meredith, Philip Glass and Groundhogs, stay for the Swedish guitar improv and experimental Andean sound collages. Plus, Stuart's featured album is Dub Housing, the second release from "the colossi of Rust Belt Avante Garage" Pere Ubu.
items.title: Pere Ubu - Dub Housing

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 9 Dec. Its the Freak Zone, 6 Music's one-stop shop for all your left-field and experimental music needs. What's on special offer this week? There's contemporary Norwegian prog, Italian experimentalism and American drone folk. plus Gong, Greg Foat and the mighty John Barry. Meanwhile Stuart's featured album is American jazz guitar giant Sonny Sharrock's 1991 masterpiece Ask The Ages.
items.title: Sonny Sharrock - Ask the Ages

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 2 Dec. Welcome to the Freak Zone, 6 Music's home for all the weird and wonderful music you didn't know you needed to hear. This week there's math rock and wonky pop, groovy sounds from Turkey and Nigeria, top tunes from Brian, Keith and Vashti, and Purcell played by a pair of top Norwegian jazzers. Plus, Stuart's featured album is Robbie Basho's masterpiece of American primitive guitar Visions of the Country.
items.title: Robbie Basho's Visions of the Country

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 25 Nov. Stuart gets spooky and supernatural for All Hallows Eve. Expect werewolves, demons, witches and a blasphemous seal. There's music from Keith Emerson, Sun Ra and France Gall plus live advice from an LA witch.

items.title: Manami

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 3 Dec. Broadcast in tribute to The Godfather of Techno, Juan Atkins. This is another chance to hear his 6 Mix from 2013. Atkins was widely regarded as one of the originators of Techno music, along with Derrick May and Kevin Saunderson. The trio, often referred to as the Belleville Three, attended high school together in Belleville, Michigan, near Detroit. Growing up, they all regularly tuned in to DJ Charles 'The Electrifying Mojo' Johnson's radio show, which has been cited as a big influence on their musical development. After being inspired by hearing electronic music fo…
items.title: In tribute to Juan Atkins

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 30 Nov. Glasgow techno pioneers Slam, aka Stuart McMillan and Orde Meikle, are in the 6 Mix celebrating 35 years of Soma Records ahead of the release of their Soma 35.4 Activate Remixes featuring Luke Slater, Oscar Mulero, Phil Berg and Nastia Reigel. Produced by BBC Audio for BBC Radio 6 Music.
items.title: Slam

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 23 Nov. Manchester-based producer Andy Stott takes over the 6 Mix on 6 Music with two hours of nostalgic romances, late-night jams and music that inspired the making of his new album, Late Loop, released on the Modern Love imprint this October. A key figure in contemporary electronic music, Stott has spent the past two decades forging a singular sound, blending dub techno, post-punk textures, dream-pop atmospheres and experimental club music. Drawing on the influences behind his first album in five years, this deeply personal selection moves between old favourites and new …
items.title: Andy Stott

He also jumps in the mix exploring groovy house sounds. Produced by We Are Grape for BBC Radio 1 Dance.

Expect music from Confidence Man, HAAi, Mall Grab and more. Sam jumps in the mix spinning tracks to showcase the pool of talent from his home country, with music from Marli, CC Disco and more. And Australian podcaster and DJ Ricky Nord provides the guest mix with 30 minutes of Aussie selections. Produced by We Are Grape for BBC Radio 1 Dance.

items.desc: Tangerine arrives on Butter Sessions with Language of Sound, the second offering from the Melbourne / Naarm-based artist Clementine Girard-Foley. Four forward-thinking tracks that nod to techno, electro, IDM and bass music, with a playful, slightly rude and quietly optimistic mood that Tangerine pulls off with ease. credits Written and produced by Clementine Girard-Foley. Mixed by Borgqueen at Syntonix. Mastered by Corey Kikos. Artwork and design by Maryos Syawish.

items.desc: Welcoming Kamome to the BSRMIX! The Tokyo-raised DJ and Vinyl Youth member spent some time in Melbourne / Naarm, where he quickly found his place in the local music scene. His eclectic selections made their way into DJ booths and onto dancefloors across town, leaving a lasting impression since his return to Japan. We're very happy to share this recording from his set at Tomoya's secret space at Strawberry Fields 2025. P.S. There are a few moments of silence in the recording, a little reminder of the unpredictable nature of these bush parties (the sound system shut down!)

items.desc: Gop Tun DJs are four friends with one obsession: creating the perfect dancefloor with lost gems and improbable classics. Caio T, Gui Scott, Nascii and Tyv started out in São Paulo in 2012 and have since built a party, a label and a festival that's become a vital movement. Following on from fronting Magic Dirt, she’s helmed solo projects – releasing her first solo album Adalita in 2011 and later All Day Venus in 2013 and Inland in 2022, amidst film composing, mentoring and a myriad of other projects. items.desc: DJ, producer and curator Edna Martínez, from Cartagena de Indias, works across the sonic worlds of the Caribbean and its diasporas. Rooted in champeta and picó culture, her practice connects sound system traditions, migrations and histories, bringing archival sounds and contemporary productions into dialogue across scenes and territories.
items.title: Edna Martinez

items.desc: From the host:'Edson Gómez, aka Eddy Jay, one of the voices of Rey de Rocha picó in Cartagena, Colombia, as champeta moved from the late ’90s into the 2000s. A look at a changing sound, where the singer, the lyrics and stories of everyday life began to move closer to the centre of the music.'
items.title: Champeta w/ Edna Martinez - Eddy Jay Special

items.desc: DJ and curator Edna Martínez, from Cartagena de Indias, presents champeta, a genre born inside the picós, the sound systems of Colombia’s Caribbean coast where music is presence, tension, gathering. It carries fragmented routes shaped by circulation and bootlegs. It becomes body, dance, code, a way of occupying a space that has never been neutral. From the host: "For this Tierra Bomba Special, I bring together the champeta of Michel, Lilibeth and Edwin El Maestro. Three voices from the island, with songs from the mid-2000s to 2010. Stories of love, heartbreak, celebration and everyday life."

nts-in-focus.about: A deeper look into the back catalogs of various artists.

items.desc: Brazilian singer Astrud Gilberto came to international attention in the mid-1960s with her English-language vocal on “The Girl from Ipanema”, recorded with Stan Getz, João Gilberto and Antônio Carlos Jobim. Its understated delivery helped bring bossa nova to a global audience, but her catalogue reaches well beyond that landmark recording. Through the late 1960s and 1970s, she moved between Brazilian song, jazz standards and pop across a run of solo albums, making space for a quietly distinctive style of her own. This In Focus explores the many sides of her work.
items.title: In Focus: Astrud Gilberto

items.desc: John Tavener (1944–2013) was a British composer known for his deeply spiritual and atmospheric music. Born in London, he studied at Highgate School and the Royal Academy of Music, emerging in the late 1960s with The Whale, an experimental composition released on The Beatles' Apple Records label. Although initially influenced by the avant-garde, his work became increasingly contemplative, drawing heavily on religious traditions following his conversion to Orthodox Christianity in 1977. Combining elements of classical composition, sacred choral music and minimalism, he developed a distinctive s…
items.title: In Focus: John Tavener

items.desc: A veteran of the globally connected avant-garde music scene, Hiromi Moritani aka Phew has been active since the late 1970s, when she was the vocalist of Osaka post-punk band Aunt Sally. Going solo in the 1980s, she began a prolific and highly collaborative career, working with Can, Jim O'Rourke, Boredoms, The Raincoats, Ryuichi Sakamoto and numerous other fellow travellers in boundary pushing music. Stylistically, her music features prominent improvisation, and aligns with post-punk, industrial, minimalism, noise and - in later years - electronic compositions. Compiled and mixed by Brian Cone…
items.tags: Post Punk, Experimental, Industrial , Art Rock
items.title: In Focus: Phew

items.desc: 60 minutes of essential pop music from Robyn, the Swedish singer, songwriter and producer whose formula for melancholic dance pop took over the charts. Selected and mixed by Lil C.
items.title: In Focus: Robyn

items.desc: American composer and synthesist, Pauline Anna Strom first began releasing music in the early 1980s under the moniker Trans-Millenia Consort. Working for the most part in isolation, she crafted immersive synth soundscapes, conjuring imagined worlds between ancient myth and imagined futures. After her early records fell out of circulation, her work was introduced to new audiences in 2017 through the compilation Trans-Milenia Music. She returned to releasing original work with the 2020 album Angel Tears in Sunlight, released by RVNG Intl just months after her passing.
items.title: In Focus: pauline anna strom

items.desc: Emerging from the creative crucible of LA's loose "beat scene" collective of the mid-2000s alongside fellow artists such as Ras G, Thundercat, and Nosaj Thing, Steven Ellison aka Flying Lotus took a painterly approach to the structure of hip hop production. Part of a jazz and soul lineage that includes Motown songwriter Marilyn McLeod and spiritual jazz matriarch Alice Coltrane, Ellison infused instrumentals with loose improvisational flourishes and an experimental spirit that frequently breaks beyond the definitions of hip hop. His style has expanded further incorporating R&B, jazz, IDM, and…
items.title: In Focus: Flying Lotus

In this RA Exchange, Dettmann talks about the long road from bedroom DJ to one of techno's leading figures: first falling in love with '80s new wave records, running a record sto…
items.title: EX.818 Marcel Dettmann

items.desc: Sun-soaked house from the Circoloco favourite. Want to know what life is like when the sun is always shining? Carlita might be able to tell you. The Istanbul-born DJ follows the summer around the world, and her calendar reads like a festival bucket list: Coachella, Sónar, Tomorrowland and, most often, Circoloco at DC-10. It's also a neat encapsulation of her DJing. One of the biggest names in big-room house, Carlita has a sound that's warm and melodic, often pairing house classics with pop hooks and the odd swell of strings. It's a long way from where she started. Classically trained on the c…
items.title: RA.1064 Carlita

items.desc: The Manchester artist marches back into the club and cranks up the subs. “You don’t need to study music, you need to study sounds.” That was the advice Andy Stott’s piano teacher, Alison Skidmore, gave him as a teenager. Around 2010, stuck in a creative rut and tired of his dub techno sound, Stott slowed things down, started sampling field recordings and brought Skidmore in as his vocalist. Records like Luxury Problems and Faith In Strangers added a pop twist to his cavernous sound and made him a critics’ darling. His new album, Late Loop, out now, is his first in five years, is out this week…
items.title: RA.1063 Andy Stott

items.desc: A sonic diary from one of UK experimental music's brightest talents. Loraine James doesn't like to sit still. She first made waves on Hyperdub, where 2019's For You and I and 2021's Reflection reimagined grime, IDM and dub with a mischievous touch. But calling her a club experimentalist has never fit the bill. The London-born artist has collaborated with everyone from Yaeji to TSVI, remixed Kelela and Tirzah, hosts an NTS show steeped in contemporary classical and turns out records at a staggering pace. She also makes some of the most evocative ambient around as Whatever the Weather. What hol…
items.title: RA.1062 Loraine James

items.desc: A 100 percent production mix from the dubwise don. “You can find inspiration in everything, as insignificant as it seems,” Andy Martin told 15 Questions earlier this year. For the Mexican-Jamaican producer, that stretches from dub to Mexican literature, ancestral knowledge and science fiction, all fed into techno that sounds otherworldly but never forgets the floor. Dub is the skeleton of Martin’s music. Sometimes it’s explicit, as on his collaboration with Lee “Scratch” Perry. Sometimes it’s subtler, as on this year’s “Tierra de Nahuales” for Animalia, where a dub siren and decayed reverb pu…
items.title: RA.1061 Andy Martin

items.desc: The Berlin DJ, one of the brightest of her generation, makes a patient case for house and techno on vinyl. We’ve all heard the phrase “DJ’s DJ.” Too often, it’s lazy shorthand for a technical skill so esoteric it’s lost on the dance floor. But Nathalie Ogazón Faber embodies the craft in its fullest sense, commanding respect from the regulars at the booth to the sound technician at the back. Known simply as Ogazón, she played her first gig in 2018 and made her Berghain debut in 2022. Since then she’s become the quintessential Panorama Bar DJ, a resident in spirit alongside ItaloJohnson, Steffi…
items.title: RA.1060 Ogazón

items.desc: Cinematic techno from the mysterious Dutch producer. Some of the best techno is both beautiful and austere. On an old Robert Hood or Sandwell District track, the industrial clank of percussion gives way to bursts of melody where you can hear the ghosts singing inside the machines. It's this version of techno that the Dutch producer nthng has been honing since the mid-2010s, from his debut on Lobster Theremin's Mörk to records for Delsin. His take on techno, borrowing from trance, dub and ambient, has always hewed close to the edge of the dance floor, that space where dancers keep their eyes s…
items.title: RA.1059 nthng

items.desc: The band Mastodon formed in 2000 in Atlanta, Georgia. They’ve won a Grammy and been nominated for 5 others, and three of their albums have debuted at #1 on Billboard’s Hard Rock charts. For most of their history, they were a four piece, made up of Brann Dailor, Troy Sanders, Bill Kelliher, and Brent Hinds. But in March 2025, Brent Hinds left the band. And later that year, he died in a motorcycle accident. For this episode, I spoke to Brann, Troy, and Bill about making the song “Your Ghost Again,” which came together in the wake of Brent’s death, and the death of Brann’s mother. Along with the…

items.desc: The music of global girl group KATSEYE might be confusing on first listen. A less-generous read might consider their songs to be rudimentary: the lyrics are mostly nonsense, the instrumentals evoke lesser 2010s pop songs, and the aesthetic can’t decide whether it’s targeted to children or adults. However, maybe the nonsensical nature of KATSEYE is also… the point? And maybe that point is tethered to early surrealist movements of the early twentieth century? On this episode of Switched on Pop, producer Reanna makes the case to Nate that KATSEYE and ADÉLA are indicative of a larger shift in pop…

Can things actually be bad, and if so, how do we define them? items.desc: Our guest this week is author Adam Voith, whose new novel, RIYL , short for "Recommended If You Like," is an at times thinly veiled memoir of the '90s Christian punk and indie scene. With echoes of Get in the Van and Freaks and Geeks, RIYL threads that delicate needle of looking back at earnest teenage corn doggery with warts and all embarrassment, tempered by the type of affection that only time and distance allow all of us. items.desc: Social media is a strange thing. Not long ago, Transmissions host Jason P. Woodbury was ⁠retweeted by famed MTV News legend Kurt Loder⁠ . Loder was sharing a repost of a viral video featuring Detroit band Protomartyr, performing their song “Jumbo’s” at a BBQ in 2011. Loder noted, "Apparently [rock & roll] actually will never die…" This week on Transmissions, I’m speaking with return guest Casey of Protomartyr, a ba…
